naming: The loader builds its IDeserializer with CamelCaseNamingConvention and IgnoreUnmatchedProperties, so a C# PascalCase property binds to the camelCase YAML key. Dictionary keys (headers, query, bodyFields, params, options) bind verbatim. Enum-like values (transport, auth.type, bodyKind, pagination.strategy, iterate kind/granularity, landing.compression, incremental.source) are parsed case-insensitively with '-' and '_' stripped before matching (YamlAcquireFlowLoader.ParseEnum), so snake_case, kebab-case, and PascalCase spellings are all accepted.
forms: An api flow declares either ONE endpoint (the single form: source.request + a top-level landing) or SEVERAL endpoints (the multi-item form: an items[] list, each entry carrying its own request/pagination/iterate/landing over the shared source connection envelope). Exactly one form is allowed. In the multi-item form, source holds only the shared envelope (transport/baseUrl/auth/reliability/options): putting request/pagination/iterate on source, or a top-level landing, alongside items is a validation error, as is combining items with incremental (the run watermark is one value per run, so multi-item flows express incrementality through each item's date-window iterate). One multi-item flow is one pipeline row that lands each item to its own raw path, so a single acquisition can feed several downstream file/pre flows and lineage stays intact.

keys.description: The flow's name and stable identity: FlowIdentity.FromName(name) derives the FlowId every run, log, and catalog row joins on, so renaming a flow yields a new identity by design. Also the run-history folder name under .sqlflow/runs/, where the incremental watermark is read back from.

The flow's execution mode, read at the document envelope (YamlDocumentLoader's probe, FlowDocument.Mode) and projected to the catalog pipeline row. 'auto' (the default) runs on schedule fires and in batch/node group runs; 'manual' reserves a working flow for direct triggers; 'disabled' deactivates a retired one (a retired source, a run-once replay) with the same exclusions and a visible 'disabled' badge. A node-scoped run can opt into includeAll ('find all') to replay non-auto descendants deliberately, and naming a flow directly always runs it.

keys.description: Optional grouping label (the source system). The catalog groups the flow's runs under it; absent, grouping surfaces coalesce to the default batch.

Declared runtime parameters: name to default value. Each becomes a template variable {name} usable anywhere templates render (request path/query/headers/body, iteration from/to, landing pathTemplate). A caller (the CLI, the control-plane trigger, or the debugger's auto-generated parameter form) can override any declared parameter per run; supplying an UNDECLARED name fails the run before the first request (typo safety).

One declared parameter's default value. An empty or null default means the parameter is REQUIRED: a run that supplies no value for it fails before any request is sent. The name must be a valid template identifier (no braces or colons).
keys.validation: YamlAcquireFlowLoader.MapParams rejects blank names and names containing '{', '}' or ':'; AcquireEngine.BindParams fails the run when a no-default parameter receives no runtime value.

keys.description: The source side of the acquisition: which transport, where, how to authenticate, what to request, how to paginate, how to fan out, and the reliability envelope. In the single-endpoint form this holds everything including request/pagination/iterate. In the multi-item form (items[] present) it holds ONLY the shared connection envelope (transport/baseUrl/auth/reliability/options), and each item carries its own request/pagination/iterate/landing; see 'forms' above.

keys.description: The transport the source speaks. http covers REST, GraphQL, and SOAP-over-POST (auth/request/pagination apply); sftp lists and downloads remote files; azuretable queries an Azure Storage Table. The non-HTTP transports carry their credentials and locators in source.options. Matching strips '-'/'_' and is case-insensitive, so azure_table and AzureTable also parse. (S3 object copy is a cpy flow, not an api transport.)

The base endpoint, interpreted per transport: an http(s) origin (https://api.acme.com), an sftp://host[:port] URL, or the Azure Table account URL. For HTTP, request.path is joined under it (base treated as a directory).

HTTP authentication. Secret material is always a ${env:...} or ${keyvault:vault/secret} reference resolved at run time, never an inline value. Ignored by the non-HTTP transports (their credentials live in source.options).

The authentication strategy. none: anonymous. api_key_header: secretRef sent in the header named headerName. api_key_query: secretRef sent as the query parameter named paramName. bearer: Authorization: Bearer <secretRef>. basic: HTTP Basic from secondarySecretRef (username) + secretRef (password). The three token-based types perform a token request described by the token block and apply the returned access token to every data request: oauth2_client_credentials (grant_type client_credentials), oauth2_refresh_token (refresh-token exchange), token_exchange (any bespoke POST-and-extract-token endpoint, including a pre-formed body held whole in Key Vault via token.rawBody).
Primary secret reference: the token (bearer / api-key types) or the password (basic). Resolved through the shared secret chain (${env:...} / ${keyvault:vault/secret}) at run time.
Secondary secret reference: the username for basic auth.
The request header carrying the api key, e.g. X-Api-Key or a non-standard X-Authorization.
The query parameter carrying the api key, e.g. token.
Prefix prepended to the header value (bearer / api_key_header).

keys.appliesWhen: auth.type is oauth2_client_credentials, oauth2_refresh_token, or token_exchange (required there)
keys.description: How to obtain and apply the access token: the token endpoint (or an OIDC discovery URL that resolves it), the request body, and how the returned token is applied to data requests.
The token endpoint URL. Required unless discoveryUrl supplies it. May contain ${...} secret references.
An OIDC .well-known/openid-configuration URL; its token_endpoint field supplies the token URL (the frida/Nordicport pattern). Takes precedence over url when set.
HTTP method for the token request.
How the token request body is encoded: form (application/x-www-form-urlencoded, the OAuth2 default) or json (e.g. Entur's {client_id, client_secret, audience} body or easypark's {refreshToken}).

The token-request body fields (grant_type, client_id, client_secret, scope, audience, refreshToken, ...). Values may be ${...} secret references and {param} templates. With basicAuthClient: true, client_id/client_secret are lifted out of the body into an HTTP Basic header.
One token-request body field. Secret references and {param} templates are resolved before sending.
A pre-formed body sent verbatim, e.g. a Key Vault secret already holding the full urlencoded form (the Kolumbus citybike token pattern). When set, body is ignored. Content type follows bodyKind.
Extra headers on the token request (e.g. an explicit Content-Type).

Authenticate the OAuth client with an HTTP Basic header (base64 of client_id:client_secret, both taken and removed from body) instead of sending them in the body (the Voi pattern). Requires client_id and client_secret in body.
Where in the token response JSON the access token lives (e.g. access_token, idToken). Dotted paths and [index] are supported.
The data-request header the resolved token is applied to. easypark uses the non-standard X-Authorization.
Prefix on the applied token header value.
Re-acquire the token for every fan-out iteration rather than once per run (issuers that scope tokens per window, the Voi pattern).

The HTTP pagination state machine. Each fetched page lands as its own raw file.

Fan-out iterations applied outer-to-inner: the cartesian product of all iterations produces one request pipeline per combination (each of which may itself paginate). Covers date windows (day-by-day backfills, hourly sub-windows, monthly re-reads), static lists (operator ids, routes, lines), and id lists discovered from a prior request (bikes -> per-bike sessions), optionally batched N-per-request.

date_window: walk from->to in granularity steps, binding fromVariable/toVariable per step (a per-run backfill window from the typed run parameters replaces from/to). list: iterate values, binding variable per element. ids_from: run idRequest, select ids with idPath, iterate them (batchSize groups ids into joined batches).
The template variable this iteration binds (e.g. operatorId, bikeId), referenced as {operatorId} in the request/landing templates.
The step size: hourly sub-windows (Voi/Ryde), daily windows (most sources), or monthly re-reads (svv index corrections).

keys.default: the incremental watermark when parseable as a date, else now-1d
keys.description: Inclusive window start: now, today, yesterday, startOfMonth, an offset (now-3d, now-2h, startOfMonth-1mo; units y|mo|w|d|h|mi), or an ISO date. A per-run backfill window (--from) replaces it for that run.
Exclusive window end; same expression grammar as from. A per-run backfill window (--to) replaces it for that run.
The variable bound to each step's lower bound; format it in templates as {window.from:yyyy-MM-dd}. Also becomes the reference date for bare date tokens ({yyyy}) within the step.
The variable bound to each step's upper bound.
The static values to iterate (operator ids, route numbers, lines).
The discovery request producing the id list (same shape as source.request: method/path/headers/query/body*). Runs once per outer-iteration combination, with the same auth.
Selects the ids from the discovery response, e.g. $[*].BikeId or $.data[*].id.
When > 1, ids are grouped into batches of this size and the variable binds to the joined batch (the svv 50-ids-per-request pattern).
The separator joining a batch of ids into the bound variable.
The reliability envelope every request runs under: timeout, retry with backoff, outbound rate limiting, a response-size cap, TLS verification, and the SSRF host allowlist.
Per-request timeout. A timeout counts as a transient transport failure for retry purposes.
Outbound request cap in requests/second via a token bucket (fractional refill, burst capped at max(rps,1)). Applied to every request including token and discovery calls.
Hard cap on a single response held in memory before landing; exceeding it fails the run with a message naming the limit.
TLS certificate verification. Disable only for a source with a broken chain you explicitly trust.

SSRF host allowlist for data requests: *.suffix matches the bare domain and any subdomain; anything else is an exact host. Private, loopback, link-local (including the 169.254.169.254 cloud metadata address), multicast, and unique-local addresses are ALWAYS blocked regardless of this list. Token/discovery calls keep the IP guard but skip the host allowlist (they are trusted config).

Non-retryable HTTP statuses that mark a single fan-out request as a tolerated SKIP instead of failing the run. A wide date x id sweep routinely carries ids the endpoint no longer accepts (a decommissioned route, a closed account), and one stale id must not cost the whole sweep; each skipped request is logged as 'acquire.skip' with the endpoint's own error body and counted in the run's skippedRequests, so a newly-broken id stays visible. Only non-2xx codes in 100-599 are accepted (a 2xx is landed, never skipped) and the retry policy still runs first, so a transient 429/5xx retries before it can be skipped.

Retry policy: exponential backoff (baseDelayMs * 2^attempt, capped at maxDelayMs) on transport failures and the transient statuses 408/425/429/500/502/503/504; any other status is permanent. A server Retry-After header (delta-seconds or HTTP-date) is honored as a floor raised to (never below) the computed backoff.
Total attempts per request (each page retries independently).
First backoff delay; doubles per attempt.
Backoff ceiling, also bounding an honored Retry-After.
Honor the server's Retry-After as a floor on the backoff (a Retry-After: 0 from a CDN edge cannot busy-loop; a huge value is capped by maxDelayMs).

Transport-specific options for the non-HTTP transports; values may be ${...} secret references. sftp: username (required), password OR privateKey (+passphrase), remotePath (default .), pattern (glob, default *), modifiedWithinDays, take (most-recent N). s3: bucket (or the s3://bucket base url), prefix, region (default eu-west-1), accessKey + secretKey (required), pattern, modifiedWithinDays, take. azuretable: tableName (required), connectionString OR accountUrl+sasToken, filter (OData, templated with iteration variables), select (comma-separated columns).

One transport option; see source.options for the per-transport keys. Secret-bearing options (password, privateKey, accessKey, secretKey, sasToken, connectionString) must be ${...} references, never inline values.

keys.default: absent (the single-endpoint form: source.request + a top-level landing)
keys.description: The multi-endpoint form: one entry per endpoint, each with its own request/pagination/iterate/landing over the shared source connection envelope (mirrors a cpy flow's steps). One flow fetches every listed endpoint and lands each to its own raw path. Mutually exclusive with a top-level landing, with request/pagination/iterate on source, and with incremental; see 'forms' above.
keys.validation: YamlAcquireFlowLoader.MapItems: items + top-level landing, items + source.request/pagination/iterate, and items + incremental each fail loading; every item requires a landing and (for http) a request.

keys.description: An optional stable label for the endpoint (e.g. bikes, alert), surfaced in run logs. Distinct across the flow's items.
This endpoint's HTTP request template. Same shape and fields as source.request (method/path/headers/query/bodyKind/body/bodyFields/contentType).
This endpoint's pagination. Same shape and fields as source.pagination.
This endpoint's fan-out iterations. Same shape and fields as source.iterate (date_window/list/ids_from).

Where this endpoint's raw payloads land. Same shape and fields as the top-level landing (target/pathTemplate/format/compression/overwrite/persistHeaders/skipEmpty/skipUnchanged/protect). Each item's landing target is the raw path a downstream file/pre flow reads, so it is the lineage join point for that endpoint.

keys.required: single-endpoint form only (required there; replaced by items[].landing in the multi-item form)
keys.description: How fetched payloads are written to the raw zone. The payload is landed VERBATIM (raw bytes, original format): no CSV conversion, no flattening (one exception: declared landing.protect rules scrub/pseudonymise the matched fields before the bytes are written); downstream json/csv/xml file flows ingest the landed files into SQL. In the multi-item form this is declared per item under items[].landing instead.

The raw-zone base location: an ADLS Gen2 / Blob URI (abfss://fs@account.dfs.core.windows.net/base or https://account.dfs.core.windows.net/fs/base, written through the shared Azure credential with no per-flow storage secret) or a local/UNC path (dev/test). Templated, then secret-resolved once per run.

The relative path under target for each payload, minus extension. Binds date tokens ({yyyy}, {MM}, {yyyyMMdd}), iteration variables ({operatorId}, {window.from:yyyy}), declared params, {page} (the page index / file name / object key), and {runId}. When two payloads render the same path in one run, the later is disambiguated with its page/item discriminator so pages never collide.

The landed file extension: auto derives it from the response Content-Type (json/xml/csv/jsonl/txt, +json/+xml suffixes honored, unknown -> bin); or set an explicit extension (json, xml, csv, txt, bin).
Optional gzip on landing (a .gz suffix is appended after the format extension).
Overwrite an existing landed file. When false, a colliding write fails the run rather than clobbering (blob ETag-guarded on Azure).
Also write a <file>.headers.json sidecar of the response headers per page, with sensitive headers (authorization, cookie, x-api-*, ...) redacted.
Skip landing a payload whose record array is empty (or whose body is empty for non-JSON), rather than writing a zero-row file. Skips are counted separately in the run result.

Skip rewriting a landed file whose target already holds byte-identical content (compared by content hash), so a fetch that returned the same file does not bump its modified time and re-trigger downstream ingestion. Set false to write every fetched payload unconditionally. No effect when overwrite is false.

Data-protection rules applied to the raw payload BEFORE it is written, in declaration order, so PII/sensitive fields are scrubbed, pseudonymised, or generalised at the acquisition boundary and never persisted raw. Format-aware: json, jsonl, xml, and csv payloads are protectable; any other landed format (or a payload that fails to parse) fails the run rather than landing unprotected. This is the ONE deliberate exception to the land-verbatim rule.

The field selector, interpreted per the landed format. JSON/JSONL: a JSON path (optional leading $, dotted properties, [*] array wildcard, [n] index), e.g. $.data[*].rider. XML: an element path starting at the document root (requests.request.rider; repeated elements match all occurrences), with an optional trailing @name selecting an attribute. CSV: the header column name. A path matching nothing is a no-op for JSON/XML; a CSV column the header lacks is an error.

The protection transform: remove (delete the field; CSV blanks it to keep the schema), redact (constant or pattern suppression), mask (partial visibility), hash (unkeyed SHA-256 hex), hmac (keyed one-way pseudonym; requires secret), tokenize (token substitution; deterministic when secret is set), encrypt (reversible deterministic AES-256-GCM-SIV; requires secret), generalize (precision reduction: dates, age buckets, zip prefixes, numeric rounding).

A ${...} reference to the key material for the keyed transforms. REQUIRED for hmac and encrypt; optional for tokenize (a keyed token is deterministic across runs, an unkeyed one is random per run). Resolved once per run through the secret resolver; the raw key never appears in YAML.

Linkability of the keyed transforms: transaction (run-scoped salt, same value maps differently across runs), relationship (salted by flow name and the optional relationship param; consistent within this source), person (no extra salt; globally consistent wherever the same key is used).
Transform mode. redact: full (default) | partial | email | phone | card. generalize: year (default) | month | quarter | decade | age_range | zip3 | zip2 | round.
redact mode=full: the constant that replaces the value.
The masking character for mask and the partial/email/phone/card redact modes.
redact mode=partial: leading characters kept visible.
redact mode=partial: trailing characters kept visible.
mask: leading characters kept visible.
mask: trailing characters kept visible.
hmac: hmac_sha256 (fast) or pbkdf2 (KDF-hardened for low-entropy values; iteration count via iterations).
hmac algorithm=pbkdf2: the PBKDF2 iteration count.
hmac: truncate the hex output to this many characters (full digest when omitted).
tokenize: the token template; {uuid} and {short} expand from the token core, any other text is a literal prefix.
scope=relationship: an extra salt label narrowing consistency to a named relationship within the flow.
generalize mode=age_range: the bucket size in years.
generalize mode=round: round to the nearest multiple of this step.
CSV payloads: the field delimiter; auto-detected from the header among ; , tab | when omitted.
Escape hatch for transform parameters not covered by the flat knobs; merged with them (flat knobs win).

keys.default: absent (the flow fetches its full declared window every run)
keys.description: Incremental resume (single-endpoint form only): the watermark is read from the flow's own run history (.sqlflow/runs, successful runs only, so a failed run never advances the mark) and advanced to the max observed this run. A full-load run (--full) ignores the stored watermark. Not valid with items[] (one watermark per run cannot serve several endpoints); a multi-item flow expresses incrementality through each item's date-window iterate.

Where the watermark is derived from. response: track the max of a response column across the run (persisted in run.json as watermarkAfter). lake: reserved for deriving the resume point from what is already landed.

The record field whose lexicographic max is the watermark (e.g. updated_at in RFC3339, where lexicographic order equals chronological, or a numeric id). Read across the records located by pagination.recordsPath.
The template variable the resolved watermark is bound to at run start, so a request can send it (e.g. since: "{lastUpdated}"). Keyset pagination reads the watermark directly and needs no binding.
The watermark used on the first run, when no prior successful run exists.
